## GPT-5 prompt contribution

OpenClaw adds a shared GPT-5 prompt contribution for GPT-5-family runs on OpenClaw-assembled prompt surfaces. It applies by model id, so PI/provider routes such as legacy pre-repair refs (`openai-codex/gpt-5.5`), `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.5`, `opencode/gpt-5.5`, and other compatible GPT-5 refs receive the same overlay. Older GPT-4.x models do not.

The bundled native Codex harness does not receive this OpenClaw GPT-5 overlay through Codex app-server developer instructions. Native Codex keeps Codex-owned base, model, personality, and project-doc behavior; OpenClaw contributes only runtime context such as channel delivery, OpenClaw dynamic tools, ACP delegation, workspace context, and OpenClaw skills.

The GPT-5 contribution adds a tagged behavior contract for persona persistence, execution safety, tool discipline, output shape, completion checks, and verification on matching OpenClaw-assembled prompts. Channel-specific reply and silent-message behavior stays in the shared OpenClaw system prompt and outbound delivery policy. The friendly interaction-style layer is separate and configurable.

| Value                  | Effect                                      |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `"friendly"` (default) | Enable the friendly interaction-style layer |
| `"on"`                 | Alias for `"friendly"`                      |
| `"off"`                | Disable only the friendly style layer       |

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Config">
    ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
    {
      agents: {
        defaults: {
          promptOverlays: {
            gpt5: { personality: "friendly" },
          },
        },
      },
    }
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="CLI">
    ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
    openclaw config set agents.defaults.promptOverlays.gpt5.personality off
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Tip>
  Values are case-insensitive at runtime, so `"Off"` and `"off"` both disable the friendly style layer.
</Tip>

<Note>
  Legacy `plugins.entries.openai.config.personality` is still read as a compatibility fallback when the shared `agents.defaults.promptOverlays.gpt5.personality` setting is not set.
</Note>

## Voice and speech

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Speech synthesis (TTS)">
    The bundled `openai` plugin registers speech synthesis for the `messages.tts` surface.

    | Setting      | Config path                                              | Default                                 |
    | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
    | Model        | `messages.tts.providers.openai.model`                    | `gpt-4o-mini-tts`                       |
    | Voice        | `messages.tts.providers.openai.voice`                    | `coral`                                 |
    | Speed        | `messages.tts.providers.openai.speed`                    | (unset)                                 |
    | Instructions | `messages.tts.providers.openai.instructions`             | (unset, `gpt-4o-mini-tts` only)         |
    | Format       | `messages.tts.providers.openai.responseFormat`           | `opus` for voice notes, `mp3` for files |
    | API key      | `messages.tts.providers.openai.apiKey`                   | Falls back to `OPENAI_API_KEY`          |
    | Base URL     | `messages.tts.providers.openai.baseUrl`                  | `https://api.openai.com/v1`             |
    | Extra body   | `messages.tts.providers.openai.extraBody` / `extra_body` | (unset)                                 |

    Available models: `gpt-4o-mini-tts`, `tts-1`, `tts-1-hd`. Available voices: `alloy`, `ash`, `ballad`, `cedar`, `coral`, `echo`, `fable`, `juniper`, `marin`, `onyx`, `nova`, `sage`, `shimmer`, `verse`.

    `extraBody` is merged into `/audio/speech` request JSON after OpenClaw's generated fields, so use it for OpenAI-compatible endpoints that require additional keys such as `lang`. Prototype keys are ignored.

    ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
    {
      messages: {
        tts: {
          providers: {
            openai: { model: "gpt-4o-mini-tts", voice: "coral" },
          },
        },
      },
    }
    ```

    <Note>
      Set `OPENAI_TTS_BASE_URL` to override the TTS base URL without affecting the chat API endpoint. OpenAI TTS is still configured through an API key; for OAuth-only live talk-back, use the Realtime voice path instead of agent-mode STT -> TTS speech.
    </Note>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Speech-to-text">
    The bundled `openai` plugin registers batch speech-to-text through
    OpenClaw's media-understanding transcription surface.

    * Default model: `gpt-4o-transcribe`
    * Endpoint: OpenAI REST `/v1/audio/transcriptions`
    * Input path: multipart audio file upload
    * Supported by OpenClaw wherever inbound audio transcription uses
      `tools.media.audio`, including Discord voice-channel segments and channel
      audio attachments

    To force OpenAI for inbound audio transcription:

    ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
    {
      tools: {
        media: {
          audio: {
            models: [
              {
                type: "provider",
                provider: "openai",
                model: "gpt-4o-transcribe",
              },
            ],
          },
        },
      },
    }
    ```

    Language and prompt hints are forwarded to OpenAI when supplied by the
    shared audio media config or per-call transcription request.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Realtime transcription">
    The bundled `openai` plugin registers realtime transcription for the Voice Call plugin.

    | Setting          | Config path                                                          | Default                                                                       |
    | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | Model            | `plugins.entries.voice-call.config.streaming.providers.openai.model` | `gpt-4o-transcribe`                                                           |
    | Language         | `...openai.language`                                                 | (unset)                                                                       |
    | Prompt           | `...openai.prompt`                                                   | (unset)                                                                       |
    | Silence duration | `...openai.silenceDurationMs`                                        | `800`                                                                         |
    | VAD threshold    | `...openai.vadThreshold`                                             | `0.5`                                                                         |
    | Auth             | `...openai.apiKey`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `openai-codex` OAuth        | API keys connect directly; OAuth mints a Realtime transcription client secret |

    <Note>
      Uses a WebSocket connection to `wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime` with G.711 u-law (`g711_ulaw` / `audio/pcmu`) audio. When only `openai-codex` OAuth is configured, the Gateway mints an ephemeral Realtime transcription client secret before opening the WebSocket. This streaming provider is for Voice Call's realtime transcription path; Discord voice currently records short segments and uses the batch `tools.media.audio` transcription path instead.
    </Note>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Realtime voice">
    The bundled `openai` plugin registers realtime voice for the Voice Call plugin.

    | Setting                               | Config path                                                         | Default                                                        |
    | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | Model                                 | `plugins.entries.voice-call.config.realtime.providers.openai.model` | `gpt-realtime-2`                                               |
    | Voice                                 | `...openai.voice`                                                   | `alloy`                                                        |
    | Temperature (Azure deployment bridge) | `...openai.temperature`                                             | `0.8`                                                          |
    | VAD threshold                         | `...openai.vadThreshold`                                            | `0.5`                                                          |
    | Silence duration                      | `...openai.silenceDurationMs`                                       | `500`                                                          |
    | Prefix padding                        | `...openai.prefixPaddingMs`                                         | `300`                                                          |
    | Reasoning effort                      | `...openai.reasoningEffort`                                         | (unset)                                                        |
    | Auth                                  | `...openai.apiKey`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `openai-codex` OAuth       | Browser Talk and non-Azure backend bridges can use Codex OAuth |

    Available built-in Realtime voices for `gpt-realtime-2`: `alloy`, `ash`,
    `ballad`, `coral`, `echo`, `sage`, `shimmer`, `verse`, `marin`, `cedar`.
    OpenAI recommends `marin` and `cedar` for the best Realtime quality. This
    is a separate set from the Text-to-speech voices above; do not assume a TTS
    voice such as `fable`, `nova`, or `onyx` is valid for Realtime sessions.

    <Note>
      Backend OpenAI realtime bridges use the GA Realtime WebSocket session shape, which does not accept `session.temperature`. Azure OpenAI deployments remain available via `azureEndpoint` and `azureDeployment` and keep the deployment-compatible session shape. Supports bidirectional tool calling and G.711 u-law audio.
    </Note>

    <Note>
      Realtime voice is selected when the session is created. OpenAI allows most
      session fields to change later, but the voice cannot be changed after the
      model has emitted audio in that session. OpenClaw currently exposes the
      built-in Realtime voice ids as strings.
    </Note>

    <Note>
      Control UI Talk uses OpenAI browser realtime sessions with a Gateway-minted
      ephemeral client secret and a direct browser WebRTC SDP exchange against the
      OpenAI Realtime API. When no direct OpenAI API key is configured, the
      Gateway can mint that client secret with the selected `openai-codex` OAuth
      profile. Gateway relay and Voice Call backend realtime WebSocket bridges use
      the same OAuth fallback for native OpenAI endpoints. Maintainer live
      verification is available with
      `OPENAI_API_KEY=... GEMINI_API_KEY=... node --import tsx scripts/dev/realtime-talk-live-smoke.ts`;
      the OpenAI legs verify both the backend WebSocket bridge and the browser
      WebRTC SDP exchange without logging secrets.
    </Note>
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Azure OpenAI endpoints

The bundled `openai` provider can target an Azure OpenAI resource for image
generation by overriding the base URL. On the image-generation path, OpenClaw
detects Azure hostnames on `models.providers.openai.baseUrl` and switches to
Azure's request shape automatically.

<Note>
  Realtime voice uses a separate configuration path
  (`plugins.entries.voice-call.config.realtime.providers.openai.azureEndpoint`)
  and is not affected by `models.providers.openai.baseUrl`. See the **Realtime
  voice** accordion under [Voice and speech](#voice-and-speech) for its Azure
  settings.
</Note>

Use Azure OpenAI when:

* You already have an Azure OpenAI subscription, quota, or enterprise agreement
* You need regional data residency or compliance controls Azure provides
* You want to keep traffic inside an existing Azure tenancy

### Configuration

For Azure image generation through the bundled `openai` provider, point
`models.providers.openai.baseUrl` at your Azure resource and set `apiKey` to
the Azure OpenAI key (not an OpenAI Platform key):

```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
{
  models: {
    providers: {
      openai: {
        baseUrl: "https://<your-resource>.openai.azure.com",
        apiKey: "<azure-openai-api-key>",
      },
    },
  },
}
```

OpenClaw recognizes these Azure host suffixes for the Azure image-generation
route:

* `*.openai.azure.com`
* `*.services.ai.azure.com`
* `*.cognitiveservices.azure.com`

For image-generation requests on a recognized Azure host, OpenClaw:

* Sends the `api-key` header instead of `Authorization: Bearer`
* Uses deployment-scoped paths (`/openai/deployments/{deployment}/...`)
* Appends `?api-version=...` to each request
* Uses a 600s default request timeout for Azure image-generation calls.
  Per-call `timeoutMs` values still override this default.

Other base URLs (public OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible proxies) keep the standard
OpenAI image request shape.

<Note>
  Azure routing for the `openai` provider's image-generation path requires
  OpenClaw 2026.4.22 or later. Earlier versions treat any custom
  `openai.baseUrl` like the public OpenAI endpoint and will fail against Azure
  image deployments.
</Note>

### API version

Set `AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION` to pin a specific Azure preview or GA version
for the Azure image-generation path:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
export AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION="2024-12-01-preview"
```

The default is `2024-12-01-preview` when the variable is unset.

### Model names are deployment names

Azure OpenAI binds models to deployments. For Azure image-generation requests
routed through the bundled `openai` provider, the `model` field in OpenClaw
must be the **Azure deployment name** you configured in the Azure portal, not
the public OpenAI model id.

If you create a deployment called `gpt-image-2-prod` that serves `gpt-image-2`:

```
/tool image_generate model=openai/gpt-image-2-prod prompt="A clean poster" size=1024x1024 count=1
```

The same deployment-name rule applies to image-generation calls routed through
the bundled `openai` provider.

### Regional availability

Azure image generation is currently available only in a subset of regions
(for example `eastus2`, `swedencentral`, `polandcentral`, `westus3`,
`uaenorth`). Check Microsoft's current region list before creating a
deployment, and confirm the specific model is offered in your region.

### Parameter differences

Azure OpenAI and public OpenAI do not always accept the same image parameters.
Azure may reject options that public OpenAI allows (for example certain
`background` values on `gpt-image-2`) or expose them only on specific model
versions. These differences come from Azure and the underlying model, not
OpenClaw. If an Azure request fails with a validation error, check the
parameter set supported by your specific deployment and API version in the
Azure portal.

<Note>
  Azure OpenAI uses native transport and compat behavior but does not receive
  OpenClaw's hidden attribution headers — see the **Native vs OpenAI-compatible
  routes** accordion under [Advanced configuration](#advanced-configuration).

  For chat or Responses traffic on Azure (beyond image generation), use the
  onboarding flow or a dedicated Azure provider config — `openai.baseUrl` alone
  does not pick up the Azure API/auth shape. A separate
  `azure-openai-responses/*` provider exists; see
  the Server-side compaction accordion below.
</Note>

## Advanced configuration

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Transport (WebSocket vs SSE)">
    OpenClaw uses WebSocket-first with SSE fallback (`"auto"`) for `openai/*`.

    In `"auto"` mode, OpenClaw:

    * Retries one early WebSocket failure before falling back to SSE
    * After a failure, marks WebSocket as degraded for \~60 seconds and uses SSE during cool-down
    * Attaches stable session and turn identity headers for retries and reconnects
    * Normalizes usage counters (`input_tokens` / `prompt_tokens`) across transport variants

    | Value              | Behavior                      |
    | ------------------ | ----------------------------- |
    | `"auto"` (default) | WebSocket first, SSE fallback |
    | `"sse"`            | Force SSE only                |
    | `"websocket"`      | Force WebSocket only          |

    ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
    {
      agents: {
        defaults: {
          models: {
            "openai/gpt-5.5": {
              params: { transport: "auto" },
            },
          },
        },
      },
    }
    ```

    Related OpenAI docs:

    * [Realtime API with WebSocket](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/realtime-websocket)
    * [Streaming API responses (SSE)](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/streaming-responses)
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Fast mode">
    OpenClaw exposes a shared fast-mode toggle for `openai/*`:

    * **Chat/UI:** `/fast status|on|off`
    * **Config:** `agents.defaults.models["<provider>/<model>"].params.fastMode`

    When enabled, OpenClaw maps fast mode to OpenAI priority processing (`service_tier = "priority"`). Existing `service_tier` values are preserved, and fast mode does not rewrite `reasoning` or `text.verbosity`.

    ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
    {
      agents: {
        defaults: {
          models: {
            "openai/gpt-5.5": { params: { fastMode: true } },
          },
        },
      },
    }
    ```

    <Note>
      Session overrides win over config. Clearing the session override in the Sessions UI returns the session to the configured default.
    </Note>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Priority processing (service_tier)">
    OpenAI's API exposes priority processing via `service_tier`. Set it per model in OpenClaw:

    ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
    {
      agents: {
        defaults: {
          models: {
            "openai/gpt-5.5": { params: { serviceTier: "priority" } },
          },
        },
      },
    }
    ```

    Supported values: `auto`, `default`, `flex`, `priority`.

    <Warning>
      `serviceTier` is only forwarded to native OpenAI endpoints (`api.openai.com`) and native Codex endpoints (`chatgpt.com/backend-api`). If you route either provider through a proxy, OpenClaw leaves `service_tier` untouched.
    </Warning>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Server-side compaction (Responses API)">
    For direct OpenAI Responses models (`openai/*` on `api.openai.com`), the OpenAI plugin's Pi-harness stream wrapper auto-enables server-side compaction:

    * Forces `store: true` (unless model compat sets `supportsStore: false`)
    * Injects `context_management: [{ type: "compaction", compact_threshold: ... }]`
    * Default `compact_threshold`: 70% of `contextWindow` (or `80000` when unavailable)

    This applies to the built-in Pi harness path and to OpenAI provider hooks used by embedded runs. The native Codex app-server harness manages its own context through Codex and is configured by OpenAI's default agent route or provider/model runtime policy.

    <Tabs>
      <Tab title="Enable explicitly">
        Useful for compatible endpoints like Azure OpenAI Responses:

        ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
        {
          agents: {
            defaults: {
              models: {
                "azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5": {
                  params: { responsesServerCompaction: true },
                },
              },
            },
          },
        }
        ```
      </Tab>

      <Tab title="Custom threshold">
        ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
        {
          agents: {
            defaults: {
              models: {
                "openai/gpt-5.5": {
                  params: {
                    responsesServerCompaction: true,
                    responsesCompactThreshold: 120000,
                  },
                },
              },
            },
          },
        }
        ```
      </Tab>

      <Tab title="Disable">
        ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
        {
          agents: {
            defaults: {
              models: {
                "openai/gpt-5.5": {
                  params: { responsesServerCompaction: false },
                },
              },
            },
          },
        }
        ```
      </Tab>
    </Tabs>

    <Note>
      `responsesServerCompaction` only controls `context_management` injection. Direct OpenAI Responses models still force `store: true` unless compat sets `supportsStore: false`.
    </Note>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Strict-agentic GPT mode">
    For GPT-5-family runs on `openai/*`, OpenClaw can use a stricter embedded execution contract:

    ```json5 theme={"theme":{"light":"min-light","dark":"min-dark"}}
    {
      agents: {
        defaults: {
          embeddedPi: { executionContract: "strict-agentic" },
        },
      },
    }
    ```

    With `strict-agentic`, OpenClaw:

    * No longer treats a plan-only turn as successful progress when a tool action is available
    * Retries the turn with an act-now steer
    * Auto-enables `update_plan` for substantial work
    * Surfaces an explicit blocked state if the model keeps planning without acting

    <Note>
      Scoped to OpenAI and Codex GPT-5-family runs only. Other providers and older model families keep default behavior.
    </Note>
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Native vs OpenAI-compatible routes">
    OpenClaw treats direct OpenAI, Codex, and Azure OpenAI endpoints differently from generic OpenAI-compatible `/v1` proxies:

    **Native routes** (`openai/*`, Azure OpenAI):

    * Keep `reasoning: { effort: "none" }` only for models that support the OpenAI `none` effort
    * Omit disabled reasoning for models or proxies that reject `reasoning.effort: "none"`
    * Default tool schemas to strict mode
    * Attach hidden attribution headers on verified native hosts only
    * Keep OpenAI-only request shaping (`service_tier`, `store`, reasoning-compat, prompt-cache hints)

    **Proxy/compatible routes:**

    * Use looser compat behavior
    * Strip Completions `store` from non-native `openai-completions` payloads
    * Accept advanced `params.extra_body`/`params.extraBody` pass-through JSON for OpenAI-compatible Completions proxies
    * Accept `params.chat_template_kwargs` for OpenAI-compatible Completions proxies such as vLLM
    * Do not force strict tool schemas or native-only headers

    Azure OpenAI uses native transport and compat behavior but does not receive the hidden attribution headers.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.
</collaboration_mode>

<apps_instructions>
## Apps (Connectors)
Apps (Connectors) can be explicitly triggered in user messages in the format `[$app-name](app://{connector_id})`. Apps can also be implicitly triggered as long as the context suggests usage of available apps.
An app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.
An installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. If `tool_search` is available, the apps that are searchable by `tools_search` will be listed by it.
Do not additionally call list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates for apps.
</apps_instructions>

# How I Work

Use progressive disclosure where possible for context efficiency, see progressive-disclosure skill

Tradeoff: These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

1. Think Before Coding
Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.

Before implementing:

State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
2. Simplicity First
Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.

Good code should read like a clear action sequence:

```ts
const harness = await init({ model });
const session = await harness.session();
const result = await session.prompt(prompt, { schema });
```

```php
Route::resource('photos', PhotoController::class)
    ->only(['index', 'show']);

Flight::where('active', 1)
    ->orderBy('name')
    ->limit(10)
    ->get();
```

No features beyond what was asked.
No abstractions for single-use code.
No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
No error handling for impossible scenarios.
If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

3. Surgical Changes
Touch only what you must. Quality improvements stay inside the task's boundary.

Reuse before adding:

Reuse existing types, utilities, hooks, components, and patterns before writing new ones.
Don't broaden public APIs unless the acceptance criteria require it.

When editing existing code:

Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When quality blocks the task:

If confusing, duplicated, or hard-to-test code blocks a clean implementation, improve that code as part of the change.
If a small local cleanup makes the implementation simpler or safer, do it and call it out (PR body / summary).
A real quality issue not needed for the change → flag it for follow-up; don't expand scope.

When your changes create orphans:
Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

4. Goal-Driven Execution
Define success criteria. Loop until verified.

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

"Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
"Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
"Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:

1. [Step] → verify: [check]
2. [Step] → verify: [check]
3. [Step] → verify: [check]
Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.

For spec-backed work:
- Keep each slice traceable to a spec section, issue, or acceptance bullet.
- Answer "what's left?" with concrete file/task deltas, not broad themes.
- After risky or architecture-heavy slices, report done, yet-to-do, spec deviations, roadblocks, and harder-than-expected parts.
- Treat review feedback as a loop: implement slice → inspect diff/comments → fix → promote repeated style feedback into AGENTS.md or the relevant skill.
- Checkpoint completed slices before starting a risky refactor.
- For gnarly threads, write a short handoff that links existing specs/artifacts instead of duplicating them.

These guidelines are working if: fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

Don’t fight errors: after the same error twice, stop and gather new evidence — local docs/source first, then web if version/API behavior is unclear — before choosing a fix.

## Cache footguns

- Keep `params.system` and `tools[]` byte-stable across same-cwd sessions.
- Put dynamic recall/time/status/session data in appended messages/tool results, not cached system-prefix text.
- Mark situational/heavy extension tools `deferLoading: true`; gate with `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:deferred-tool-contracts`.
- Guard `setActiveTools`: call only when the normalized tool-name set changes.
- Prefer `tool_reference` / provider-native `defer_loading` over mutating active tools after `tool_search`.

## Gates

- Extension/profile/cache surface: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`.
- Fork/core surface: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`.

<!-- end import: /Users/luke/Projects/agent-scripts/pi-dev.md -->

## Code Quality

- Follow `/code-craft` for naming, composability, progressive complexity, chainable APIs. Load explicitly for new APIs or elegance refactors.
- Excellent pattern worth preserving → propose adding to `/code-craft`, log in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Execution Policy

- Clear + reversible → act. Irreversible/destructive/private/external (send/post/delete/deploy) → ask first.
- One non-retrievable decision blocking safe progress → ask one concise question. Don't stack three.
- Newest user instruction wins conflicts.

## Tool Discipline

- Prefer tool evidence over recall for action, state, or mutable facts.
- Smallest native parser: `jq` for JSON; `Read` for files; `Grep` for known text. Avoid Python one-liners.
- Expensive/remote commands: run once, save to `/tmp`, inspect saved file. Don't re-run.
- Concrete path from user → try `Read`/image view before asking. Let tool errors provide evidence.
- Known file region → default to `offset`/`limit`; read the whole file when broader context is needed.
- Parallelize independent retrieval; serialize dependent/destructive/approval-sensitive steps.
- Long-running commands: use the harness wake primitive, not repeated wait/poll/sleep loops. In Pi, `bash run_in_background:true` runs a command detached and re-invokes you when it exits; use it for one-shot “wait until done” commands. `monitor_start` streams events from a background process; each stdout line is a notification, so use it for one wake per actionable event.
- Waiting strategy: foreground `sleep` is blocked. To wait on a condition, use Monitor with an until-loop. To wait for a command you started, use `run_in_background:true`. For possibly hung work, use one long fallback check; for external state (CI, deploys, remote queues), emit sparse state-change lines matched to actual cadence.
- Before claiming success: smallest meaningful gate (test, typecheck, lint, build, screenshot, diff).
- **Verify before deciding:**
  - Classifying an issue → cite a concrete artifact (log line, test output, file:line, actual-vs-expected diff).
  - Writing a fix → list integration points it relies on (config, hook, codepath, data shape) and verify each exists.
  - Test: *what evidence would change my mind?* Can't answer → don't have enough yet.
- **3-strike rule**: same tool + same input 3+ times → stop. Write (1) what you know, (2) what's unknown, (3) a different action.

## Agent & Tool Routing

Pi subagent types (`explore`/`general`/`worker`/`reviewer`/`plan`/`decompose`) → see `pi-AGENTS.md`. Claude Code agents → `/agents`.

- Read-only multi-file investigation → exploration agent. Implementation/mixed → general-purpose. Diff review → reviewer. Design-before-code → plan.
- Known file/symbol/error, ≤3 files → direct tools, no agent.
- Children have ZERO context: brief with file paths, what's ruled out, why it matters. Never "based on your findings, fix the bug" — that pushes synthesis onto the child.
- Model/thinking routing:
  | Work | Model floor | Thinking floor |
  |---|---|---|
  | File/symbol scouting, broad read-only map | fast ok | low/off |
  | Mechanical edits in known files | medium/smart | low/medium |
  | Tests/failing CI with concrete errors | smart | medium |
  | Planning, implementation plans, API design, sequencing, migrations | frontier/strongest practical | high |
  | Code review, diff review, completion audit | smart; prefer frontier when consequential | medium |
  | Adversarial review, architecture, security, data-loss, gnarly multi-system bugs | frontier/strongest practical | high/xhigh |
  | Broad repo audit | fast scouts ok; final judgment smart/frontier | high for final |
- Never use fast/mini models for review, adversarial review, architecture judgment, security, or completion audits. Fast is for scouting, not judgment.
- **WebFetch**: known URL → fetch. GitHub URLs → prefer `gh` CLI. ~15-min cache. Only URLs seen in messages or prior search results work.
- **WebSearch**: info past cutoff, current events, version-specific docs. Include year for freshness. Skip for stable knowledge.
- **Pipeline**: `WebSearch` → pick URLs → `WebFetch` deep content. Comparing three? Search first.
- **Anti-bias**: default pull is toward `general-purpose` + `WebSearch` (look thorough). Resist. Cheap-and-narrow beats expensive-and-fuzzy.

## Skill Auto-load

Load the matching skill **before** the first tool call in that domain. Auto-trigger isn't reliable; load explicitly. Skills carry canonical commands (wrappers, gotchas, RBAC limits) that bare runbooks omit. If a skill applies, load it before giving domain-specific guidance; don't claim a skill was used unless actually loaded.

| Touching… | Skill |
|---|---|
| `kubectl`, k8s, `lue-kube`/`bermont-kube`, pods, Flux, Helm, exec/shell/logs into pods | `k8s` (use `kube` / `kube-exec` / `kube-shell` / `kube-logs` wrappers, not raw `kubectl`) |
| New API, public surface, refactor for clarity | `code-craft` |
| Agent-safe architecture hardening, godfiles/godfunctions, swarm lanes, repo scorecards | `agent-native-hardening` |
| TDD, test seams, mocks, integration vs unit | `testing` |
| Effect (TS/Node) — adopt into existing repo, or new Effect-first project | `effect` (router → `effect-incremental-adoption` / `effect-new-project`) |
| Frontend / design / UI craft | `frontend` (or named child) |
| Audit/profile a React app's render perf, locate wasted re-renders (Next.js, Vite, Remix) — measure, don't guess | `frontend` → `react-scan` child; run `react-scan init` |
| Browser automation, scraping | `browser-toolkit` |
| Architecture decision records, `docs/adr`, durable non-obvious trade-offs | `adr` |
| CI/release/versioning SDLC surface, `VISION.md`, repo automation, clean-checkout workflow | `project-sdlc` |
| Wrapping up / shipping / PR | `go` |
| Orca-managed worktrees/workspaces, visible agent lanes, terminal steering | `orca-cli` |
| Language server queries (TS/Go/Rust) | see `docs/lsp.md` |

Runbooks that prescribe raw long-form commands are reference-only; the skill's wrappers win.

## Docs & Skills Hygiene

Spot stale docs/skills/contradicting instructions while working: **fix small things in place** (typos, stale paths, old command forms, broken links); **surface for approval** when non-trivial, cross-cutting, or behavior-shifting; **ask** when intent is unclear. Don't silently ignore the rot.

## Completion Contract

- Task incomplete until every requested item handled or explicitly marked **[blocked]** with the specific missing input.
- Don't return partial work as done. Either ship, or surface the blocker plainly: *"items 1–3 done; 4 [blocked]: need <X>"*.
- Before declaring done: requirements met, claims grounded, format honored, safety preserved.
- For code/artifacts: smallest meaningful gate (see Tool Discipline). If no gate can run, say why.

## Z/L Continuum — Code Review Tiers

Classify every change at top of reply. Critical = load-bearing heart of *this* session. Unclear → ask *what here would hurt most if subtly wrong?*

| Tier | Scope | Handoff |
|---|---|---|
| **critical** | Core behavior of what's shipping now | Stop per diff, show, wait for approval. **One critical → one cycle. Never chain.** |
| **important** | Adjacent features, cross-cutting refactors, non-obvious intent | Batch diffs, summarize (files, change, tradeoff), wait for "go" |
| **routine** | Tests, fixtures, docs, lint/format, codegen, styling | Proceed. Report at end. |

- Ambiguous → classify **up** (= important). User can override any time; honor without re-litigating.

## Communication

- Correctness over voice. Style never trumps answer/format/safety.
- Lead with outcome. Cite concrete artifacts (paths, commands, errors).
- Narrate before meaningful tool use — one sentence, then call in same turn. Skip for routine reads.
- "On it" / "next up I'll…" → tool call in same turn, not more prose. Pausing? Say so.
- If blocked waiting for Luke on something attention-sensitive — especially auth, 1Password, npm/release gates, approvals, or a decision while he may be distracted — use `sag-luke` to speak a short unblock request aloud, then write the same request in chat. Example: `sag-luke --volume 0.65 "Luke, I need 1Password approval for the npm release."`
- Keep spoken prompts brief, specific, and rare. Don't use `sag-luke` for routine progress updates or non-blocking status.
- Clarify with the `AskUserQuestion` tool (not prose) when a wrong assumption would waste work — ambiguous scope, a planning fork, `grill-me` interrogation, or any either/or decision. Give 2–4 concrete options per question; an "Other" free-text choice is added automatically.
- One round of questions, then proceed on the answers. Skip it for trivial or reversible choices → just act.
- If you don't understand why the user denied a tool call, ask them with `AskUserQuestion`.

## Parallel Execution

- Independent tasks → parallel. Dependent → sequential.
- High-volume output (logs, test suites, large files) → delegate to agent or background; keep verbose out of main context.
- Multi-agent: communicate via temp files / inter-agent tools, not large chat payloads.

## Long Session Hygiene

- Few results from search → re-run with narrower scope.
- Refactors >5 files → start with exploration agents in parallel, then verify integration points before editing.
- Architecture-heavy slice drift → report roadblocks, spec deviations, harder-than-expected parts, done/yet-to-do.
- Gnarly thread crossing sessions/tools/local patches → write a `/tmp` handoff with suggested skills and artifact paths; don't duplicate specs.

## Instruction Style

- State what to use, not what to avoid.
- Assume competence. Instruction budget is finite.
- One term per concept across the file.
- Concrete input/output examples over prose rules.
- Editing LLM guidance (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, skills, prompts, tool schemas) → load `context-engineering/references/instruction-refiner.md`, then apply.

## Learning

Capture failure patterns: failure mode, detection signal, prevention rule. Use `~/Projects/agent-scripts/prompts/learning-scars.md` when documenting.
Format: `- YYYY-MM-DD: "lesson" (context) → SCARS/<issue>.md`

# my-pi Agent Instructions

This repo is Luke's personal pi extension and harness lab.

## Priorities

- Keep boot context small; move detail into focused docs under `docs/`.
- Prefer source-backed research before changing pi behavior.
- Add custom Pi functionality in `my-pi` as an extension or pi package first.
- Patch `pi-mono-fork` core only when documented extension/package APIs cannot achieve the behavior.

## Key docs

For setup/runtime changes, update catalog YAML plus governed docs when behavior changes; generated files under `docs/pi-setup/generated/` are scanner-owned.

New refs: `docs/release-engineering.md`, `docs/config-layering.md`.

## Session Briefing Card

`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/00-pi-active-context.md` — compact (≤1500 tok) briefing card injected on every session start via dream-memory harness. Covers: claude-bridge provider config, active projects, pi extensions, openclaw separation, active-memory/dreaming behaviour.

- Named `00-` → loads first in lex-sort, guaranteed within the 8-file cap.
- Keep under 6 kB. Update when project focus or runtime config changes.
- Do not add timestamps or session-specific content (breaks LLM cache).
- Format: stable markdown tables and bullets — no counters, no dates.

## Pi Context Block (session-start memory)

`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/MEMORY.md` is the single file auto-injected every session (≤1500 tokens, cache-stable). It contains:
- **Preferences & Policies** (refs to detail files)
- **Infrastructure** notes
- **Pi Stack** — fork, extensions, packages, claude-bridge, active-memory, dream
- **Active Projects & OpenClaw** — high-traffic repos + openclaw env separation

Dream upserts individual H2 sections when relevant events accumulate. Manual updates are fine; keep the file under ~5.8 kB to stay within the token budget. Regenerate the Active Projects section when the project mix shifts significantly.

## pi-memory — CC `extractMemories` parity (2026-05-30)

Write side is now per-turn extraction matching Claude Code's `extractMemories` (the 2026-05-16 "trigger gating" rev wrongly put `autoDream`'s 24h/5-session cadence on the *extraction* path — reverted). See `docs/memory-systems-comparison.md` and `docs/memory-architecture.md`. **Extraction fires at `turn_end`, per-turn**, throttled by `PI_MEMORY_MIN_NEW_TURNS` (default 1 = CC every-turn), bounded by `maxTurns: 5` (`PI_MEMORY_MAX_TURNS`) + `maxOutputTokens` (`PI_MEMORY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, default 2048). **No time/session gate on extraction** — the 24h/N-session consolidation cadence belongs to dream-memory (CC `autoDream`). Removed: `PI_MEMORY_MIN_HOURS`, `PI_MEMORY_MIN_SESSIONS`, `PI_MEMORY_SCAN_THROTTLE_MS`, the `detectPriorityBump`/`force` path, `PI_MEMORY_TURN_END_TRIGGER`. Kept as deliberate deviations from literal CC: lock as a pure **write mutex** (`~/.pi/agent/memory/.consolidate-lock-<scope>`, PID body, mtime no longer state) guarding `MEMORY.md` against concurrent same-scope forks, and **pollution skip** (`web_search`/`mcp_*`/`WebFetch` etc. disqualify the session; threshold `PI_MEMORY_POLLUTION_THRESHOLD`, default 1). Shutdown flush still runs as a final extraction. `maxTurns` is a new fork-core agent-loop primitive (see `docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`). Active-recall default OFF; opt-in via `DREAM_ACTIVE_RECALL=1`. Freshness caveats (≥1 day) wrap stale memories before injection.

## Pi Change Workflow

Use this before modifying `my-pi` or `pi-mono-fork`:

1. Read the local Pi docs above for the touched surface.
2. Choose extension/package first; write a short note if core changes are unavoidable.
3. Run Matt Pocock's architecture review lens: `~/Projects/agent-scripts/skills/matt-pocock/references/improve-codebase-architecture.md`.
4. For broad changes, anchor slices to the relevant spec/goal doc and report concrete remaining deltas.
5. Make one incremental simplification when it is local, safe, and directly adjacent to the change.
6. Update `docs/pi-setup/catalog/*.yaml` and governed docs for setup/runtime changes; never hand-edit `docs/pi-setup/generated/`.

## Workflow and subagent routing matrix

Use this matrix when spawning agents from Workflow scripts, `Agent`, or extension-owned forks. Prefer explicit routing over inherited expensive defaults.

| Work type | Agent alias | Model hint | Thinking | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read-only file/code search, broad triage, “where/how/which” | `explore` | always `fast` (never bump to `medium`, regardless of breadth) | `low` | No edits. Parent only needs conclusions, not dumps. If a read-only task needs more reasoning than `fast`, route to `plan` — do not silently upgrade `explore`. |
| Design/options/risks before implementation | `plan` | `medium` | `low`/`medium` | Read-only architecture/planning artifact. |
| Diff/regression/correctness review | `reviewer` | `medium` | `medium` | Ask for `VERDICT: PASS|FAIL|PARTIAL`. |
| Scoped implementation with known files | `worker` | `medium` unless truly critical | `medium` | Use an isolated workspace for write-capable agents. |
| Mixed search+edit+verify or shell-heavy execution | `general` | `medium`; explicit flagship only for load-bearing hard bugs | `medium`/`high` | Avoid for pure read-only work. |
| Workflow default subagent, no explicit route | omit alias | `medium` | inherits current fork setting | Workflow `agent()` defaults unspecified `model` to `medium`; pass `agent: "explore", model: "fast"` for cheap read-only fan-out. Workflow cannot directly override thinking until `ctx.forkAgent` grows that generic option. |

## Cache Stability (mandatory for fork + extension work)

Any change touching `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors **must** review the `pi-cache-stability` skill first. Anthropic prompt cache only helps when the prefix is byte-identical and alive within TTL — pi forks and extensions break this constantly without realising. The skill captures the L1/L2/L3 levers (`context: "slim"|"none"`, `systemPrompt` override, `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL=1h`), the audit checklist, and the verification recipe. Source-of-truth doc: `docs/cache-strategy.md`.

## Pre-PR local review

Before opening, updating, or declaring a PR ready, run a local review pass against the diff.

**PR gate (run order):** `codex-review` → `code-craft-pr` → `matt-pocock/improve-codebase-architecture` → `docs-freshness-pr` (wire through `pr-pipeline-orchestrator`); resolve all Tier 1/2 findings and file Tier 3 as GitHub issues. This gate is the `.github/pull_request_template.md` checklist in both `my-pi` and `pi-mono-fork`.

**Autonomous lane (the same gate, unattended):** my-pi is a ClawSweeper *target*. `.github/workflows/valkyriweb-clawsweeper-dispatch.yml` forwards issues/PRs/comments/pushes to the `valkyriweb/clawsweeper` engine via `repository_dispatch` using the personal `valkyriweb-clawsweeper` App (not bermont's); the engine (not this repo) runs review, repair, and auto-merge on its own `lue-clawsweeper` runner pool. This repo carries only the thin dispatcher — no review brain. Onboarding (App scope + `CLAWSWEEPER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secret + engine `config/target-repositories.json` entry) and the reusable shape live in `project-sdlc/references/autonomous-review.md`.

Review lenses:

- Extension/package-first: custom behavior belongs in `my-pi` extensions or pi packages unless the PR proves core is required.
- Local Pi docs: PRs that touch extension/package/SDK/core surfaces cite the relevant file under `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/`.
- Matt Pocock architecture lens: run the `improve-codebase-architecture` reference and record any accepted/deferred deepening opportunity.
- `instruction-refiner`: prompt, AGENTS.md, skill, tool, and other model-facing instruction changes.
- `code-craft`: non-trivial code, public API shape, names, reader flow, data movement, module boundaries, and needless abstraction.
- Dedup / lean-down: repeated extension glue, scripts, prompts, package metadata, docs, helpers, or package boundaries.
- Docs / evals: behavior, runtime, setup, prompt/context, or recall changes need matching docs and tests/evals.
- `agent-ci`: run local GitHub Actions CI and fix failures before handoff.

Use:

```bash
npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --quiet --all --pause-on-failure
```

If paused, fix the issue and retry with the emitted `retry` command. Do not report work as done until agent-ci passes or a real blocker is named.

Stop before PR if review finds a real P1. Fix it or document why it is intentionally deferred.

## Review guidelines

- Flag P1 when custom functionality lands in `pi-mono-fork` core without evidence that extension/package APIs cannot support it.
- Flag P1 when a Pi setup/runtime change skips catalog YAML, governed docs, or the architecture review lens.
- Flag P1 when model-facing instructions add vague guidance, duplicate rules, stale links, or long rationale that should be compressed or moved to a focused doc.
- Flag P1 when code obscures the reader flow: vague names, hidden data movement, needless abstraction, grab-bag helpers, or public APIs that make the simple path complex.
- Flag P1 when extensions, scripts, docs, package metadata, or prompts duplicate the same concept and should share one package, helper, or documented source of truth.
- Flag P1 when prompt/context changes can affect recall, tool routing, cache stability, or session startup cost without matching tests/evals/docs.
- Flag P1 when runtime/setup changes skip `docs/pi-setup/` catalog updates, governed docs, or relevant runbooks.
- Treat docs typos, broken links, and stale command examples as P1 when they affect agent behavior or setup safety.
- Prefer follow-up notes over findings for speculative extraction; require concrete repeated use or a clear package boundary before recommending shared packages.

## Verification

Before changing runtime extension behavior, run the relevant eval or add one if none exists.

- When installing, adding, modifying, or removing Pi extensions/packages, run the my-pi extension checks and the fork cache gate together:
  - `npm run test:extension-gate`
    - Includes profile cache contracts, prompt-health fixtures, claude-bridge cache markers, dream-memory cache tests, skill/tool search, native aliases, Agent view, and task tools.
  - `npm run test:skill-loader:smoke`
  - `npm run test:tool-search:smoke`
  - `npm run test:prompt-health`
  - `npm run test:claude-bridge:cache`
  - `npm run test:dream-memory:cache`
  - `npm run test:agent-view:smoke`
  - `npm run test:task-tools:smoke`
  - `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`
- Treat a failing `pi-mono-fork` build/cache gate as a blocker for extension rollout; extensions must pass against the fork they ship with.

# Pi Cache Stability

Anthropic's prompt cache is prefix matching: cache hits require the request prefix to be **byte-identical**, use the same model, include the same tools in the same order, and still be **alive within TTL**. Pi forks and extensions break this constantly without realising. Keep them honest.

**Source-of-truth**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` — read it before changing anything load-bearing.

**Project memory pointer**: `~/.pi/agent/memory/project/my-pi/project_cache_strategy.md`.

## When this skill applies

Load this skill any time you are about to:

- Add or modify a call to `ctx.forkAgent()` in a pi extension.
- Edit `forkAgent`, `_forkAgentFromExtension`, `runChild`, `resolveContextPolicy`, `buildSystemPrompt`, or `overrideBaseSystemPrompt` in `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent`.
- Build a new background agent that runs many times per session (memory extractor, advisor probe, autoresearch worker, condensation fork).
- Investigate "why is this slow / expensive" on a child agent.
- Touch the system prompt order, project context cascade, or skill loader.
- Add or revise model-facing tool APIs, schemas, `promptSnippet`, or `promptGuidelines` (also read `context-engineering/references/model-facing-api-design.md`).
- Change `pi-claude-bridge` cache config.

## Cache laws

1. **Static first, dynamic last.** Stable system prompt + tool schemas first; project context next; session context/messages last.
2. **Use messages for updates.** Dates, file-change reminders, mode changes, and run status belong in the next user/tool message, not in the cached system prompt.
3. **Do not change models mid-session.** Caches are per-model. Use a subagent handoff instead of switching the parent from Opus/Sonnet to Haiku or vice versa.
4. **Do not add/remove tools mid-session.** Tool definitions are cached prefix. Model state transitions as tools/messages, not schema swaps.
5. **Forks must share the parent prefix.** Compaction, summarization, skill execution, and side computations should reuse the parent's system prompt, tools, and context policy unless the cost is intentional.
6. **Anything that adds content writes to the dynamic boundary, never the static one.** Per-turn or per-session content (advice, status, time, memory recall, reminders, mode banners, run state) must be appended *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint — a trailing `role:"user"`/custom message — never into `systemPrompt`/`systemPrompt:build`/`params.system`/`tools[]` (the static, cached prefix). This is agnostic to the source: it holds for fork-core prompt construction, the harness, the bridge, extensions, and any future injector. The only allowed static-prefix writes are (a) deterministic, value-independent edits (e.g. stripping the volatile `Current date:` line) and (b) one-shot, memoised, byte-stable session-start blocks (e.g. dream-memory's memoised `profile-base`). Test: if the bytes can differ between two turns of the same session, it belongs in the dynamic tail.

## The three layers (in order)

| Layer | Lever | Effect | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L1** | `forkAgent({ context: "slim"\|"none" })` | Skip parent transcript / project context / skills / agent-append. Prefix shrinks ~6-8×. | `"fork"` (back-compat) |
| **L2** | `forkAgent({ systemPrompt })` | Hand-built byte-stable prompt. Cache hits across **every cwd, every session** for the same agent. | unset |
| **L3** | `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL=1h` (claude-bridge) | Cache lives 1h instead of 5min. | `1h` (already on) |

L1 and L2 compose. L3 is automatic when traffic routes through claude-bridge.

## L4 — mid-session updates via a trailing message, never the prefix (measured 2026-05-29)

Changing `params.system` (skill index `<available_skills>`, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array **mid-session** bursts the **entire conversation cache** down to the stable-system anchor — measured 100%→43% hit when pi's skill index grew by one turn (`my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`, exp1-4 through claude-bridge).

- Keep the skill index + `tools[]` **byte-stable** within a session. Tools: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder mid-session (Anthropic: a tool-set change invalidates the whole conversation cache).
- Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget/env updates as a **trailing message after the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint**, not by editing the system prompt. Use a `role:"user"` text block (model-agnostic, proven 99% warm). Opus-4.8 also accepts a `role:"system"` message immediately after a user turn (no beta header) — same cache numbers, model-gated, no extra benefit.
- Won't fix: tool-set churn (use `defer_loading`), model switch (use subagent handoff).

## Mandatory checklist before merging fork/extension changes

- [ ] **Where does the system prompt come from?** If it's auto-built from parent context, it mutates per session — cache rarely hits. Override with `systemPrompt` or accept the cost knowingly.
- [ ] **Are there per-session substitutions in the system prompt?** (slug, sessionId, paths, timestamps, file lists.) Move them to the user prompt. The system prompt must be byte-stable.
- [ ] **Is prompt order static → dynamic?** System prompt/tools first, project context next, session messages last. No dynamic values before shared stable blocks.
- [ ] **Does this change the model or tool set mid-session?** Use subagent handoffs, mode tools, system-reminder messages, or deferred tool stubs instead.
- [ ] **What is the child's `context` mode?** Default is `"fork"` which inherits the bloated parent prefix. For a focused tool-running child, use `"slim"` or `"none"`.
- [ ] **Is output capped?** A 3-tool child shouldn't burn 1800 output tokens of Opus prose. Pass `maxOutputTokens`.
- [ ] **Is it routed through claude-bridge?** Confirm `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL` is set (default `1h`).
- [ ] **Did you measure?** Capture a real jsonl after the change. Turn 1 should show `cacheRead / (cacheRead + cacheWrite) ≥ 0.8` once the cache is warm. If turn 1 is still 90% `cacheWrite`, something is mutating between calls.

## Cache-killers to grep for

When auditing an extension or a system-prompt change, search for these patterns — each is a likely cache-buster:

- `new Date()` / `Date.now()` / ISO timestamps near the front of any prompt
- Per-session counters, sequence numbers, run ids in cached blocks
- File modtimes / sizes / hashes in cached headers
- `${cwd}` / `${slug}` / `${sessionId}` substitutions inside system-prompt templates
- Skill registry growing/shrinking (any change → all downstream cache invalid)
- Tool definitions added/removed/reordered mid-session
- Model changes inside the same parent conversation
- Plan/read-only mode implemented by swapping tool sets instead of messages/tools
- Project context cascade re-read on every call

If you find one in a hot path, either:
1. Move it to the **tail** of the prompt (after the last cache breakpoint), or
2. Move it into the **user message**, or
3. Model the state change as a tool/message while keeping schemas stable, or
4. Document why it's there and what the cache cost is.

## Reference patterns

**Stable extractor** (cross-session, cross-cwd cache):
```ts
// Module-level — load once
const STABLE_SYSTEM = loadPrompt("extractor-stable-system.md");

await ctx.forkAgent({
  prompt: buildUserPrompt({ slug, sessionId, paths, ... }), // dynamic data here
  context: "none",
  systemPrompt: STABLE_SYSTEM,                              // byte-identical forever
  maxOutputTokens: 800,
  allowedTools: [...],
});
```

**Per-cwd-per-day stable** (lighter touch, no hand-built prompt):
```ts
await ctx.forkAgent({
  prompt: ...,
  context: "slim",         // skip transcript/project-context/skills, keep agent-append
  maxOutputTokens: 800,
});
```

**Existing parent-cache reuse** (default, lowest discipline):
```ts
await ctx.forkAgent({ prompt, ... }); // context defaults to "fork"
```

**Cache-safe compaction / summarization fork**:
```ts
await ctx.forkAgent({
  context: "fork",              // reuse parent prefix intentionally
  prompt: `${COMPACTION_PROMPT}\n\nSummarize the session for continuation.`,
  systemPrompt: undefined,       // do not swap to a special summary prompt
  maxOutputTokens: SUMMARY_BUDGET,
});
```

**Mode changes without tool churn**:
```ts
// Keep tool schemas stable. Send state in the next message/reminder.
await session.addUserMessage(`<system-reminder>Plan mode is active. Read and plan only; do not edit files.</system-reminder>`);
```

**Deferred tools instead of removal**:
```ts
// Keep lightweight stubs stable in the prefix; load full schemas only when selected.
const tools = stableToolStubs.map((tool) => ({ ...tool, defer_loading: true }));
```

## Quota / caller forensics

Use this section when the trigger is **"who is burning Claude quota?"** or **"why did cache_write spike at HH:MM?"** — not for byte-level cache divergence (use Anthropic diagnostics below for that).

### Workflow

1. **Scope to the current bridge run.** Never analyze the full `~/.pi/agent/logs/claude-bridge.log` by default — old runs poison the picture. The bridge usage report script scopes to the latest `Claude Bridge listening` line; pass `--history`/`--all` only when explicitly investigating long-term trends.
2. **Hit `/top-callers` first.** `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9100/top-callers | jq` gives rolling 5m + 1h totals per caller with `requests`, `input`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, model, and `meta.{source,piSessionId,title,cwd,pid,childAgent,parentSession}`. The cluster bridge exposes the same endpoint inside `claude-bridge` pods.
3. **Attribute the spike.** Pick the caller with the largest `cacheWrite` in the relevant window. `meta.cwd` + `meta.pid` + `meta.title` identifies the live Pi session. `meta.childAgent=true` means a subagent — trace `meta.parentSession` for the owner.
4. **Compute hit rate per caller.** Healthy: `cacheRead / (cacheRead + cacheWrite) ≥ 0.8` once warm. Per-caller ratio below 50% with high `cacheWrite` = that session's prefix is mutating (system prompt, tools, model, or earlier messages changed mid-run).
5. **Correlate with bridge request id.** Every `/v1/messages` log line carries `request=<uuid>` and the response returns `x-bridge-request-id`. Use it to pin a specific cache-miss to a specific Pi turn.

### Cache marker placement (the 4-marker budget)

Anthropic gives the bridge 4 cache breakpoints per request. The correct placement is:

1. System prefix
2. Tools
3. **Previous** cacheable message (so the prior assistant turn enters the rolling prefix)
4. **Latest** cacheable message

Marking only system + tools + latest message is the classic bug — long conversations then reuse only the stable system/tools anchor and rewrite the changing transcript body every request. Symptom: repeated `read=<stable anchor>` with `write=80k–150k` on a long Opus session.

### Anti-patterns observed in the wild

- **Inferring session identity from `msgs/tools/read` triplet.** A stable `read=21149` is the bridge/system/tools anchor shared across many callers, not a session id. Use `meta.piSessionId` from `/top-callers` or the bridge `request=` uuid.
- **Treating a stable `read=<anchor>` with large `write` as "server-side cache failure".** It usually means "only the prefix is cached because marker placement is wrong" — see above.
- **Continuing forensic prompts on Opus while the bridge has no caller telemetry.** Each forensic turn worsens the incident. Stop, add telemetry, restart investigation. If `/top-callers` is missing or returns empty `meta`, the Pi client isn't sending bridge headers — that is the first thing to fix.
- **An `id:"unknown"` caller in `/top-callers` with empty `meta:{}`** means *something* is hitting `/v1/messages` without sending `x-pi-*` headers — a non-Pi script, a stale Pi binary from before the telemetry rollout, or a probe. Hunt it down via the bridge log `request=<uuid>` of one of its requests, then `lsof`/`ps` on the PID to identify the client. Don't let it linger — it pollutes attribution.
- **Mirror runtime changes everywhere.** Any bridge change must land on: MacBook launchd bridge, Mac Mini, lue-kube cluster bridge, Paperclip runtime, Multica runtime. Missing one runtime makes attribution lopsided and forensics misleading.

### Required Pi → bridge headers

Every `claude-bridge`-routed Pi request must send:

- `x-pi-session-id`
- `x-pi-session-title`
- `x-pi-cwd`
- `x-pi-pid`
- `x-pi-source` (`interactive` | `child-agent` | `extension` | ...)
- `x-pi-child-agent` (`true`/`false`)
- `x-pi-parent-session` (when child)

See `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/sdk.ts` for where these are attached.

### Related scar

- `~/Projects/agent-scripts/SCARS/issue-09-claude-bridge-cache-marker-telemetry.md` — full incident write-up. Read it before any quota-attribution work.

## Routine cache inspection (run these first)

When the trigger is **"check pi caching performance"** or **"why is my usage climbing?"**, run all three before deep forensics. Cheap, deterministic, rule out the common false leads.

### 1. Bridge cache TTL — verify the path, not just the env var

The bridge defaults to `1h` **in code**: `const CACHE_TTL = (process.env.BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL || "1h")` (`pi-claude-bridge/index.js`). So an **unset `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL` is normal and not a bug** — do not chase it. Confirm the extended-cache path is actually live instead:

```bash
grep -n 'BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL\|extended-cache-ttl' ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge/index.js | head
# Live beta header on requests (1h cache only applies when this beta is sent):
grep -m1 'extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11' ~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge/index.js
```

Only flag TTL if the env var is set to something other than `1h`/`true`, or the `extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11` beta isn't being pushed onto the request.

### 2. System prompt byte-identity across sessions

A fresh session in a warm cwd **should** read the shared system+tools anchor (~40k) from a sibling's cache. Turn-1 `read=0` / 100% `write` means the anchor diverged byte-for-byte. Usual culprit: the session-start `<persistent-memory>` injection (dream-memory `dispatchSessionStart`) differs because memory/inbox files changed between the two session starts, or a `time-context` block crossed an hour boundary. Hour-stable, file-stable starts share the anchor; anything that mutates `profile/`/`inbox/` between starts splits it.

```bash
# Steady-state hit% per active session in this cwd (low hit + high write/turn = thrash):
for f in $(ls -t ~/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-luke-Projects-personal-my-pi--/2026-*.jsonl | head -5); do
  echo "== $f"; pi-cache-stats "$f" --steady 20 2>&1 | grep -E 'steady|active turns'
done
```

A brand-new session showing turn-1 0% is expected and self-heals from turn 2; only investigate if it **stays** low (system prompt is mutating every turn — see cache-killers).

**Now automated** — the bridge fingerprints every request (short sha256 of `system`, `tools`, `persistentMemory`, `projectContext`, `skills`) and exposes `/cache-divergence`. Don't eyeball diffs; ask the bridge which block split:

# Pi development deep reference

Read when changing Pi core/fork internals, extension/profile membership, config layering, native tool definitions, or cache-sensitive prompt/tool behavior.

## Golden rule: no behavior delta in core; route through the platform layer

The fork is ~228 commits ahead of upstream (`earendil-works/pi-mono`) — the goal is **not** to keep it at upstream shape, it is to keep every commit classifiable and the rebase surface shrinkable. Three tiers (grep-verified against upstream):

- **upstream-native** (zero maintenance): `pi.on(event,…)` event bus, `registerTool`, `registerFlag`/`getFlag`, `getActiveTools`/`setActiveTools`, `deepMergeSettings`, `<project_context>` block. Build freely.
- **platform delta** (good, generic, low rebase surface — these are *Luke's own* primitives, **not** upstream): the hooks/filters layer (`addFilter`/`applyFilters`/`removeAction`/`addAction`/`ExtensionHooksAPI`), the cache-split (`splitSystemPromptForCache`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY`), the `systemPrompt:build` filter, `<system-context>` carrier, agent subsystem, OTEL. They ride on top of the upstream `on()` bus. Write new platform primitives generically so they can be upstream-PR'd (each PR shrinks the rebase surface). Tag in `pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` as `… (platform)`.
- **behavior delta** (forbidden as inline core patches): any opinion about what pi *does* — prompts, tool logic, agent behavior, Luke-specific routing. Route via extension + hook/filter, never inline in `pi-mono-fork` core.

Put customization in an **extension + hook/filter** (wrap+spread a core tool def to override its fields — pattern: `native-tool-overrides` wraps `createEditToolDefinition`). No hook exposes what you need? Add a *new* hook/filter to core (sparingly — each is rebase surface), never an inline behavior patch. Log any unavoidable core change in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`. Workflow: `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md`. Fork-hygiene ADR: `my-pi/docs/adr/0004-fork-hygiene-extract-via-existing-hooks.md`. Active program: `my-pi/docs/goals/goal-2026-05-30T07-50-47Z-pi-platform-program.md`.

## Native tools (Claude-style aliases)

Registered by `my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts` (not core — wraps the fork's lowercase factories: capitalized names, arg repair, deferred loading). **Cache-critical: deterministic, one schema per capability — never add/remove/reorder mid-session.**

- Always-loaded: `Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Agent`, `Grep`. Deferred (schema on demand): `BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`. Bridge-only markers: `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`.
- Smoke test: `node extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## Tool-input ergonomics

Models call from priors, not your schema → mismatched shapes cause a validation-error loop that burns turns (and on Anthropic can poison the session). Two fixes, **do both**:

1. Make the declared schema the shape the model already reaches for — flat top-level fields over nested wrappers, expected field names, inline example, optional non-essentials.
2. Coerce tolerantly at the boundary, validate strictly inside — one `normalize…()` helper that unwraps legacy wrappers / `JSON.parse`s stringified args / maps aliases.

Keep the *declared* schema cache-stable; coerce in `execute`, not by mutating `tools[]`. Reference impls + full rationale (incl. Claude Code `TaskCreate` parity): `my-pi/extensions/task-tools/src/schema.ts` (`normalizeTaskDraft`), `native-tool-overrides` Edit `prepareArguments`.

## Profiles

A profile = manifest package selecting which extensions (→ hooks/filters/tools/commands) load. Each builds a different system-prompt prefix + tool set → **membership is cache-critical; keep deterministic.**

- `full` (`my-pi/packages/my-pi-full`) local daily driver · `harness` (`…/my-pi-harness`) headless, forbids agent-ui/human-ux · `pod` (`…/my-pi-pod`) minimal k8s/server.
- Per-extension selection, classified (`category` + `profiles`, enforced `forbiddenCategories`) in `my-pi/scripts/check-profiles.mjs`. Load a hook in only some profiles → split it into its own extension, or gate its `pi.hooks.addFilter`/`pi.on` registration on a profile/env flag.

Deep detail: `my-pi/docs/config-layering.md`.

| Layer | Name | Mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Capability | extension source defaults | `const DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 5` |
| L2 | Membership | profile manifest `pi.extensions[]` | including/excluding an extension |
| L3 | Tuning | `settings.json` `extensionConfig{}`, deep-merged global ← project | `extensionConfig["cache-base-prompt"].extendBase = true` |
| L4 | Override | env var / CLI `--flag` via `registerFlag`/`getFlag` | `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1` |

- Keep defaults in extension-owned config files or typed source defaults; keep operator tuning in `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` in `settings.json`; use env vars only as L4 overrides for one-off runs, secrets, CI, or emergency flips.
- New extension settings go in `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` in `settings.json` — never new top-level `Settings` keys, never env-only configuration.
- `getExtensionConfig(namespace)` accessor on `ExtensionAPI` is the missing ~15 LOC piece (`createExtensionAPI` has no settings handle yet — `loader.ts:254`); track as `fork-first (platform)` until upstreamed. Until it lands, extensions may read `settings.json` directly, then apply env overrides.

## Cache & system-prompt stability

**#1 footgun: changing `params.system` (skill index, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array mid-session bursts the WHOLE conversation cache** — only the stable-system anchor survives. Keep skill index + `tools[]` byte-stable: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder mid-session. Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget updates as a trailing `role:"user"` text block *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint.

- Any change to `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors passes the cache-stability review first.
- **Cross-cwd base-extend lever: `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1`** (set in `~/.zshenv` — zsh never sources `~/.profile`, so a copy there is dead). `cache-base-prompt` ext relocates the dynamic boundary so the global AGENTS chain + `<available_skills>` ride **block0** (cross-cwd shared base, cached once) instead of per-cwd **block1** (re-cached per project) — moves ~14K tok cross-cwd, `tools[]` unchanged, content-preserving. Pattern: `tool-search`; `advisor` now guarded too.
